title: Blasting and Drilling
body: Explosives are LSR 8. A single deviation on Approved Blaster authority, exclusion-zone discipline, or contraband control turns a routine blast into a fatality risk — and the June 30 audit already found real gaps sitting underneath: an unquantified redrill cost and no formal root-cause layer above the daily spreadsheet.
keyPoints: Only the named Approved Blaster on the Blasting Permit initiates the shot. No field substitution — if the Blaster isn't available, blasting stops, period.
Contraband box sits at least 15 m clear of the demarcated block. Phones, smoking materials, and ignition sources stay out — no "just checking my phone" exceptions inside the perimeter.
Exclusion zones during initiation: 300 m for personnel, 500 m for vehicles. Hold the line even when tie-up clearance is running late — that's exactly when people start drifting back in early.

Redrill rate is running ~3.4% (~2,430 of 72,000 m in June) with zero cost tracking. Every redrill is a JackRig cost, not billable to the client — flag causes as you see them (loose ground, wet/collapsing holes, fall-back material) so they can actually be categorized.
Post-blast heave — like Block 157 on June 30 — needs geotech sign-off before anything develops into that area. Don't wave it through as normal fragmentation.
apply: Stemming material stock is exhausted (~20 m³ short). If any crew is prepping the 611-614 cluster for charging, confirm stemming is physically on hand before they start — not after they've already opened holes.
